a: Supervised learning trains on labeled input-output pairs.
Unsupervised learning finds structure without labels (e.g. clustering).
Overfitting fits training data too closely and fails on new data.
Underfitting is too simple to capture the real pattern.
Hold out a test set to estimate generalization.
Cross-validation rotates folds to get a more stable score.
A feature is an input variable used by a model.
A label is the target value the model should predict.
Loss measures how wrong predictions are during training.
Gradient descent updates weights in the direction that reduces loss.
